QUESTIONS

Useful things to know.

Can we review a specialist before starting?+

The selection process can include a skills review and interview appropriate to the assignment.

Who manages day-to-day work?+

For staffing, the customer normally directs the assignment. For managed delivery, HeyDock owns the agreed delivery process. We define this before starting.

Are all roles immediately available?+

Availability is confirmed against the role and start date. We do not promise every skill is available at all times.

IN MORE DETAIL

Remote staffing or managed delivery: which do you need?

Remote technical staffing adds agreed expertise to a customer-directed team. Managed delivery gives HeyDock responsibility for the process and agreed outputs. Both models can involve remote engineers, software developers, testers, AI specialists or customer support staff, but supervision and accountability differ. The contract should reflect how the work will actually operate.

A role brief should describe the technology stack, skill level, language, working hours, reporting line and expected tasks. It should also identify the equipment and secure access needed to work. Candidate review can then focus on relevant skills rather than a generic job title that means different things to different teams.

Remote chat and customer support need approved knowledge, escalation and quality review. An engineer working on infrastructure needs clear permissions and change control. A developer needs repository access, acceptance criteria and a release process. Agreeing these details before onboarding helps the specialist contribute without unnecessary access or ambiguous responsibilities.
